mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A holds below-average possession (consistent with their away-venue profile and Team B's possession dominance) AND Team A's foul rate is at or above competition average. Measure Team A yellow cards in that joint cell versus the marginal baselines.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A yellow cards rise when possession deficit and foul rate are jointly elevated, beyond the additive expectation from each observable separately.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession dominance (structurally higher than Team A and above competition baseline) combined with Team A's elevated foul rate against opponents jointly predicts a higher yellow-card accumulation for Team A, beyond what either observable alone would suggest. When a lower-possession team commits fouls at an above-average rate against a possession-dominant opponent, disciplinary pressure compounds.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint two-observable conditioning (possession deficit × foul rate) for Team A simultaneously, not a single observable against one coarse band. Neither possession alone nor fouls alone captures the compounding disciplinary mechanism.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Within matches, condition on Team A's full-match foul rate being above competition average AND measure whether cards_2h FOR Team A is disproportionately elevated relative to competition baseline cards_2h. The half-level split on cards_2h combined with full-match foul rate creates a within-match state dependency.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A second-half cards rise with higher full-match foul accumulation in a non-linear (threshold-like) fashion, with the relationship stronger for Team A than Team B given their asymmetric card profiles.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half card rate (cards_2h FOR) is structurally elevated relative to Team B's, and Team A concedes more fouls against them in recent matches. The joint relationship between Team A's first-half foul accumulation and their second-half card rate — conditioning on both observables simultaneously — tests whether early foul load predicts a non-linear escalation in second-half disciplinary events.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This combines a within-match period split (second-half cards) with a full-match continuous observable (fouls) for the same team, and tests an asymmetric cross-team comparison — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B concedes a high shots volume (above their ALL_PRIOR mean) and measure whether corner kicks FOR Team A co-vary with that shots-against surge. The joint conditioning on shots-against volume AND shots-on-target-against ratio distinguishes volume-driven from quality-driven defensive pressure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's shots-against volume is elevated relative to their shots-on-target-against (i.e., high volume but lower conversion to on-target), Team A's corner kick generation rises with shots volume but the relationship saturates as shots-on-target-against increases — indicating a non-linear joint dependency.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-against have surged sharply in recent matches (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) while their goals-against have also risen, yet their shots-on-target-against remain relatively stable. This divergence between shots-against volume and shots-on-target-against — a joint relationship between two distinct defensive observables — tests whether Team B's recent defensive deterioration is driven by volume conceded or by quality conceded, with implications for corner kick generation by Team A.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct opponent-side defensive observables (shots-against and shots-on-target-against) and a third attacking observable (corners), not a single observable against one band. The recent-vs-prior divergence for Team B adds a regime-shift dimension.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint half-level profiles: Team A scores disproportionately in the second half (second-half goals FOR > first-half goals FOR) AND Team B concedes at a relatively even or slightly second-half-weighted rate. Measure whether total second-half goals in such matchups exceed the competition baseline second-half goal rate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal volume rises when a team with a strong second-half scoring skew (Team A) faces an opponent whose defensive half-split does not compensate — the joint half-level asymmetry compounds toward elevated second-half scoring.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals-for show a pronounced first-half vs second-half asymmetry (0.493 vs 0.920 per match), while Team B's goals-against show a first-half vs second-half asymmetry in the opposite direction (0.613 vs 0.653). The joint within-match half-level split across both teams' goal-timing profiles — conditioning on both simultaneously — tests whether the match's goal distribution is skewed toward the second half beyond what either team's individual half-split would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on both teams' within-match half-level goal splits — a two-dimensional within-match state dependency — not a single observable with one coarse band. The asymmetry is cross-team and cross-half, not reducible to either team's half-split alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B holds above-average possession (above competition baseline of 50%) AND measure Team A's offsides-for rate. Compare this joint cell against Team A's unconditional offside rate and against matches where possession is more balanced. The venue dimension (home) interacts with possession level as a second conditioning dimension.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's offside rate is suppressed when facing a possession-dominant opponent at home, with the suppression deepening as opponent possession rises above a threshold — a non-linear relationship between opponent possession level and the attacking team's offside frequency.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides-for are structurally lower at home than away (1.027 vs 1.559), while Team B's possession dominance (52.6% overall, 56.2% recent) suggests they will control territory. The joint relationship between Team B's possession level and Team A's offside rate — conditioning on both simultaneously — tests whether high-possession opponents suppress the attacking team's offside-triggering runs (a proxy for high-line attacking intent) in a non-linear way, with Team A's home offside rate already below their away rate suggesting a venue-possession interaction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint conditioning on two distinct observables (opponent possession level as a continuous variable and Team A's offside production) with a non-linear/threshold dependence on possession, plus a venue interaction — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.
